ranking.note: Raised to P1: removes the cs_main dependency from index sync, fixes startup/reindex races, and is the prerequisite for out-of-process indexing (#10102) and rescan reuse (#15719) — unblocks several others, so it cannot sit level with ordinary cleanups.
Raised to P1 and moved up six places: an index that answers 'transaction does not exist' on a disk/corruption error is exactly the silently-wrong-answer case this category ranks first.
Kept P2 rather than joining #35728 in P1 because the bulk of the change lives in coins/dbwrapper, which this category treats as validation; its index benefit is secondary.
Placed ahead of #26966 because it extracts the batching foundation that the parallel-sync PR builds on.
Moved down five places: a brand-new index type with an external consumer is the last-listed concern in this category, below integrity fixes and sync-time work on indexes users already run.

inconsistencies: Chain: #34489 (batched index writes) is stated foundation work for #26966 (parallel index sync); review #34489 first or the parallel work will be rebased twice.

Overlapping scope: #24230 reworks how indexes reach node state and own their sync loop, while #35474 moves index ownership from globals into NodeContext. They touch the same ownership/plumbing surface; settle #24230's interface direction first so #35474 does not relocate globals that #24230 removes.

#35728 and #34132 both attack 'read/deserialization failure looks like a missing record'. #35728 is index-scoped and directly fixes the user-visible false 'not found'; #34132 generalizes the policy in dbwrapper and deletes CCoinsViewErrorCatcher. Review #35728 first, then check #34132 does not re-introduce a second error path for the same condition.

#36002 (pruned txindex) and #36480 (txospenderindex compact keys) both depend on the key-format work merged in #35531 and both aim at pruned-mode support; the block-sequence helper refactor is shared, so coordinate which PR lands the shared helper.
result.notes: Band spread is deliberate: two P1s for data-integrity/unblocking work, a broad P2 middle covering the user-facing feature, sync-time and disk-footprint work, and P3/P4 for ownership plumbing, directory housekeeping and the format-string cleanup. #34132 sits partly outside this category's boundary (coins/dbwrapper is validation here) and was banded on its index-facing consequence only.
